gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much daily sun each camera needs. The makers' own figures put it at about 10 minutes for the Reolink Go PT Ultra and about 2 hours for the eufy S330, a 12× gap. Reolink's 21.6 Wh battery would refill from empty in 3.6 hours of full sun at its 6 W panel's rated output.
standout_why: I compared against three rival pages. Buffalo Alarm (cited) gives prices and data-plan ranges but no battery or panel figure for any camera. Reolink's own 4G solar guide (cited) gives 21.6 Wh, the 6 W panel and '10 minutes a day', but no refill-time figure and no comparison with eufy. SecurityCamHQ (top result) gives no panel wattage or battery figure for the Go PT Ultra or the eufy S330. None of them sets the brands' daily-sun claims side by side or works out a battery-to-panel ratio.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's 'best overall' pick of the Reolink Go PT Ultra for remote, shaded or winter sites. By the makers' own figures it needs about one-twelfth the daily sun of the eufy S330 and runs about twice as long on one charge (about 2 months against about 1 month). The eufy is still the choice when Wi-Fi fallback matters, but it needs a spot with roughly 2 hours of direct sun a day.

findings.label: Full-sun hours to refill from empty (rated output)
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra (Reolink US product page)
findings.note: 21.6 Wh ÷ 6 W = 3.6 h. This is a lower bound: it ignores charging losses and assumes the panel reaches its rated 6 W.

findings.label: Maker-claimed daily sun need and runtime per charge
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra (Reolink US product page)
findings.note: Quotes: 'Just 10 minutes of charging a day is enough' and 'lasts for about 2 months per charge'. Implied average draw: 21.6 Wh ÷ 60 days ≈ 0.36 Wh/day. Replacing that at 6 W takes 0.36 ÷ 6 × 60 ≈ 3.6 min of rated output, so the 10-minute claim leaves room for losses. Reolink doesn't say what usage the runtime claim assumes.

findings.note: No voltage or Wh is given, so I could not compute Wh per panel watt or a refill time.

findings.label: Maker-claimed daily sun need and runtime per charge
findings.value: about 2 h of direct light/day; about 1 month per charge
findings.note: Quote: 'about 2 hours of direct light a day keeps the battery charged'. The runtime claim assumes 10 motion events and 5 live views a day at moderate temperature. Compared with Reolink: 120 min ÷ 10 min = 12× the claimed daily sun, and about 1 month ÷ about 2 months = half the runtime per charge (the two brands' usage assumptions differ).
